item.content:encoded:
Italy's Meloni approves tougher anti-riot laws after Milan violence Reuters | Updated: 20-10-2026 23:57 IST | Created: 20-10-2026 23:57 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Italy approved a raft of security measures on Tuesday including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration, tougher penalties for rioters, and financial liability for parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting. The move came after unrest swept northern Italian cities at the weekend, including the financial capital Milan, where gangs of mainly young people went on the rampage, smashing windows, robbing shops and attacking police. "There is nothing revolutionary about vandalising and stealing. Vandalism and theft are not protest, they are criminality," Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on social media, unveiling the decree. As part of the package, which comes into immediate effect, anyone who takes part in a group of at least five people and endangers public safety during protests faces up to five years in prison and a maximum fine of €20,000 ($22,460). Penalties increase if faces are concealed or people injured. Authorities are empowered to order prompt compensation for any damage inflicted and, in the case of minors, their parents will be held liable. Police will be allowed to detain youths aged between 14 and 17, even if they have not committed a crime, provided there is evidence they pose a danger, extending powers that previously applied only to adults. While authorities fear further unrest at demonstrations planned for Saturday, the government said it would deploy 500 army troops alongside the police in Milan until the end of 2026. The military will help reinforce security at key sites, step up surveillance of sensitive locations and enhance monitoring across the area, the defence ministry said in a statement. MELONI'S SECURITY CRACKDOWN The disturbances in northern Italy echoed riots in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent turmoil in years. Meloni has passed a steady stream of security crackdowns since taking office in 2022, which critics say do little to address the underlying causes of crime and disorder. Italy's prison population has increased by more than 17% over four years, or nearly 10,000 people, government data shows. Meloni's government is also facing mounting pressure from a separate wave of protests in southern Italy, where truck drivers angered by soaring diesel prices and the rising cost of living have staged roadblocks that are disrupting supply chains. Some pasta makers have had to halt production and agricultural groups have warned that fruit and vegetables could be left to rot. The government has promised fresh aid for road hauliers after talks with industry representatives. Protesters in both the north and the south say rising prices are pushing families into poverty -- a concern for Meloni ahead of national elections that are due in 2027. "We know what it means to look for a job, to earn an insufficient wage, and to see no prospects for the future ... but hardship must never be used as an excuse for violence," the prime minister said on Tuesday. ($1 = 0.8906 euros) (Editing by Gavin Jones and Crispian Balmer)

Iran tells Pakistan army chief no talks with Washington until demands are met Reuters | Updated: 20-10-2026 23:32 IST | Created: 20-10-2026 23:32 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iran told Pakistan's army chief on Tuesday that there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, Iranian media reported, underscoring its hardening stance despite mediation efforts by key interlocutor Pakistan. President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts and regional developments with Field Marshal Asim Munir in Tehran, according to Nournews. Pakistan is a key intermediary between the United States and Iran. Earlier mediation efforts helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the Islamabad Memorandum quickly unravelled as fighting between Iran and the US resumed weeks after. Munir also met Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who said Washington could not regain Tehran's trust until it fulfilled seven conditions Iran set last month for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, according to an Iranian readout of the meeting. The demands include ending a US blockade on its ports, the lifting of sanctions on its oil exports as well as ending hostilities on all regional fronts. Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, delivered a similar message during a separate meeting with Munir, saying there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, according to Iranian media. Rezaei also said all enriched nuclear materials would remain in Iran, reiterating Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei's position that near-weapons-grade uranium should not be shipped abroad. US Vice President JD Vance said earlier this month that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' eight-month-old war. Israel, the United States and other Western states have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, including pointing to its move to enrich uranium to 60%, far higher than needed for civilian uses and closer to the 90% needed for a weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons.

item.content:encoded:
WRAPUP 4-Zelenskiy meets Witkoff as US-Ukraine relations sink to new lows Reuters | Updated: 20-10-2026 22:24 IST | Created: 20-10-2026 22:24 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was meeting US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday in a bid to rescue relations that have sunk to new lows as Donald Trump has courted Moscow and Kyiv has complained about Washington withholding vital defences. Zelenskiy and Witkoff clasped one another in a hug as they went into the talks hosted by the leaders of Norway and Finland in Oslo. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner was attending remotely. Zelenskiy held talks with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere and Finnish President Alexander Stubb ahead of his meeting with the US delegation. Zelenskiy, Stoere and Stubb are due to hold a press conference after 1700 GMT. TRUMP HAS CALLED FOR ZELENSKIY TO BE REPLACED Kyiv says Washington has lately failed to provide early warning of Russian missile launches, throttled SpaceX's Starshield satellite links that guide Ukrainian drones, and failed to deliver air defences paid for by European allies. Western European countries view defending Ukraine from Russia's invasion as an existential issue and have strongly backed Zelenskiy, seeking to head off a deeper rupture between Washington and Kyiv. Washington denies deliberately hindering Ukraine's war effort. But Trump, who has waived sanctions on Russia in what he says is an effort to lower US fuel prices, has repeatedly rebuked Zelenskiy, and called for him to be replaced. In the latest comments expressing warmth towards Moscow and coldness towards Kyiv, Trump said on Monday: "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." He said Zelenskiy, who has rejected Russia's maximalist conditions for ending its war, was "not helping matters much", and that Kyiv should find "somebody else to negotiate". RUBIO SAYS US MISSILES MAY NOT HAVE BEEN DELIVERED YET US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged on Tuesday that a consignment of US air defence missiles bought by European countries for Ukraine may not have been delivered, but denied that the US had changed policy. "The important takeaway for you is that there has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," he told journalists during a visit to India. The Kremlin said it was hoping to set up a meeting soon between Witkoff and Russian President Vladimir Putin, an indication that Witkoff could make the latest of several visits to the Kremlin after meeting Zelenskiy. As US ties with Ukraine have deteriorated, Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukrainian cities, particularly targeting power stations and fuel, despite a call from Trump for both sides to spare each other's energy systems. Russia bombarded cities in western Ukraine overnight, targeting electricity systems and knocking out power across swathes of the country that had previously been spared. Ukraine held back for several days last week from hitting Russian oil refineries in deference to Trump's request, but has resumed strikes after Russia showed no sign of complying. Both sides have also struck data centres. Trump has repeatedly condemned Ukrainian attacks on Russia while saying little about Russia's far more severe attacks on Ukraine, which have grown even more deadly as Kyiv says US support has been withheld for its air defences. RUSSIAN ATTACKS Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday it struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and two other cargo vessels en route to Odesa. Russian forces also hit two logistics hubs, it said. Ukrainian officials said a Russian drone had struck near a petrol station on a highway heading south from Kyiv on Tuesday, killing three people and setting cars ablaze. An attack on a warehouse near the capital also killed three. Footage released by Ukraine's emergency services showed firefighters battling a huge blaze, surrounded by twisted wreckage. Two people were killed in a Russian attack on storage areas outside the southeastern city of Dnipro, the regional governor said. Four other people were reported killed in Kramatorsk in the east. Energy facilities were attacked in seven Ukrainian regions overnight, knocking out power, and the western Lviv region was struck again during the day. Russian drones also struck an energy facility in Kyiv on Tuesday, mayor Vitali Klitschko said, with authorities saying power was out in four districts. ZELENSKIY SPEAKS TO RUBIO Zelenskiy said he had spoken with Rubio about ballistic missile interceptors, early warning of Russian attacks and "the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored". "Of course, all of this comes against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this horrific war and the constant killing of people," Zelenskiy said in a post on X. The deterioration of relations began 10 days ago when Trump lifted sanctions on Russian diesel in a deal agreed with Putin, which he said would help reduce prices. High fuel costs since Trump launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans before midterm legislative elections on November 3. Over the weekend, Trump issued a broad waiver for tougher sanctions on Russia that were meant to have begun this week. Washington denies withholding intelligence from Kyiv or imposing curbs on Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink communications system. Kyiv says the satellite receptors no longer work when mounted on fast-moving objects such as drones. SpaceX boss Elon Musk has said Starshield is controlled by the US government and any limits on its use are ultimately up to Trump. The United States under Trump has largely stopped providing weapons to Ukraine but lets European countries buy them on Kyiv's behalf. It also provides intelligence and technology that Europe cannot match.

GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks mostly rise as oil, US yields ease; euro edges up Reuters | Updated: 20-10-2026 22:23 IST | Created: 20-10-2026 22:23 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US stocks rose as oil prices and Treasury yields eased on Tuesday, while the euro inched higher even as worries about unrest in France remained. Helping the Dow, 3M shares gained sharply after it said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon . Shares of the industrial conglomerate were also higher after it raised its full-year profit forecast. Quarterly earnings are due from SpaceX and Netflix after the US market closes, with results from AI heavyweights such as Meta and Tesla scheduled later in the week. Investors are looking to corporate earnings for evidence that consumers and the broader economy remain resilient, but also that massive AI spending is paying off. Reflecting some of this nervousness was a 32% drop in South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group, when the stock fell below its initial public offering price in its market debut. Investors are also still assessing the risk that higher interest rates pose to AI stocks. "This is a market relieved that rates have come down, relieved that there's less volatility in oil prices, even though they remain elevated," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. "Earnings season can distract this market. Earnings season can give this market reason to go higher," he said. US Treasury yields dropped, with economic data showing slumping demand for US housing. Traders see a 14.9% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike of at least 25 basis points at its policy meeting next week, according to CME FedWatch, down from 22.1% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier. The Commerce Department said US single-family homebuilding and permits for future construction fell sharply in September, while the National Association of Realtors said its pending home sales index tumbled 7.3% to 66.0 last month, the lowest level since the series started in 2001. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note dropped 4 basis points to 5.096%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 490.46 points, or 0.94%, to 52,453.89, the S&P 500 gained 30.54 points, or 0.4%, to 7,721.27 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 53.23 points, or 0.2%, to 26,484.11. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe added 0.93 points, or 0.08%, to 1,130.91. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.14%. European semiconductor companies including ASML and ASMI were lower. French stocks fell 0.4%. EURO EDGES UP, OIL DOWN France's cities were calm overnight under curfews imposed after last weekend's unrest, as protest groups announced a new round of demonstrations next Saturday. The euro was up 0.17% at $1.1229. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.22% to 101.75. France's government bond yields climbed further on Tuesday, with investors remaining cautious ahead of the plans for further protests. The unrest in France has underscored the difficulties the French government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's 10-year OAT yield was up 3 basis points at 4.96%; it reached 4.9937%, its highest since July 2002, in early October. The yield gap between OATs and Bunds widened by 5.5 bps to 152.50 bps. Oil prices slipped after touching a five-month high during a choppy session as traders weighed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. US crude fell 0.89% to $102.74 a barrel and Brent dropped 1.2% to $108.23 per barrel.
